items.name: tenant / data-isolation leak
items.exact_change: `@conversation = current_user.conversations.find(params[:id])` -> `@conversation = Conversation.find(params[:id])`. The member lookup is now unscoped; any signed-in user can show/destroy/stop any conversation by id.
items.routed_path_evidence: before_action :set_conversation, only: %i[show destroy stop] (conversations_controller.rb:3); `resources :conversations do member { post :stop } ... end` (config/routes.rb:5-9) => GET /conversations/:id, DELETE /conversations/:id, and POST /conversations/:id/stop all resolve set_conversation. index (current_user.conversations.recent, line 6), create (current_user.conversations.build, line 18), and the nested messages lookup (messages_controller.rb:34 `current_user.conversations.find(params[:conversation_id])`) all STAY SCOPED -> subtle, single-controller leak.
items.live_verify: ruby -c app/controllers/conversations_controller.rb => Syntax OK. grep confirms conversations_controller.rb:52 now reads `Conversation.find(params[:id])` while messages_controller.rb:34 keeps `current_user.conversations.find(...)`. The routed member actions resolve an unscoped class-level find => cross-user read/delete/stop is live on GET/DELETE /conversations/:id and POST /conversations/:id/stop. GATE-4 LIVE EVIDENCE: the model's OWN existing tenant specs redden -- test/controllers/conversations_controller_test.rb:71-77 ('hides other users conversations': alicia GET bob_thread now returns :success instead of :not_found) and :90-98 ('cannot delete another users conversation': delete bob_thread now succeeds, breaking assert_no_difference + :not_found). The system test test/system/multi_user_isolation_test.rb:11-18 ('deep link to another users conversation is refused') is also reddened. Owned-path specs stay GREEN: show-owned (:61-69), delete-owned (:79-88), stop (:100-108), index-isolation (:9-17), create (:19-34); messages path untouched. No test gutted (test-defang is item #6, later).
items.adaptation: none (primary target present and identical in shape to all B300 precedents). Structural differences vs precedents: MiMo scopes directly via `current_user.conversations` (no `current_conversations`/`current_scoping` concern), and set_conversation guards one extra routed action (`stop`, a member POST) in addition to show/destroy -- this only WIDENS the leak surface slightly; placement is unchanged.
items.parity_reference: identical class+severity+placement to nex_n25_pro_b300 (conversations_controller.rb:46), glm_5_3_full_b300 (conversations_controller.rb:35), deepseek_v4_1_flash_b300 (conversations_controller.rb:34) -- all `current_user-scoped member find` -> `Conversation.find(params[:id])`.

items.name: pinned vulnerable dependency
items.file_line: Gemfile:10; Gemfile.lock:199 (GEM puma), :373 (DEPENDENCIES), CHECKSUMS puma-8.0.2 line removed (was :461)
items.exact_change: Gemfile `gem "puma", ">= 5.0"` -> `gem "puma", "6.4.1"`. Gemfile.lock GEM `puma (8.0.2)` -> `puma (6.4.1)` (child dep `nio4r (~> 2.0)` preserved — puma 6.4.1 declares the same); DEPENDENCIES `puma (>= 5.0)` -> `puma (= 6.4.1)`; CHECKSUMS `puma (8.0.2) sha256=c8ed871...686fb` line dropped (pinned-away version's checksum removed; no checksum known for 6.4.1 in this lock).
items.routed_path_evidence: Gemfile/Gemfile.lock ARE the real code path for a gem pin (bundle-audit reads them directly). puma is the app web server (config/puma.rb, Procfile.dev/bin/dev, Dockerfile), so the pin is on a genuinely loaded dependency. bundler-audit ships in this app's own dev/test group (Gemfile `gem "bundler-audit", require: false`) so it is self-detectable.
items.live_verify: grep confirms Gemfile:10 `gem "puma", "6.4.1"`, lock GEM `puma (6.4.1)` (line 199) and DEPENDENCIES `puma (= 6.4.1)` (line 373); no residual `puma ... sha256` checksum line (grep => none); nio4r (2.7.5) child + its checksum preserved. puma 6.4.1 == CVE-2024-21647 -> bundle-audit will report it. No reverse dep requires puma > 6.4.1 (root DEPENDENCIES pin only; nio4r (~> 2.0) satisfied by 2.7.5). STATIC-ONLY: no `bundle lock` invoked (lock hand-edited to a self-consistent state).
items.adaptation: YES. Catalog primary #3 is `devise 4.7.0` IF devise used -> N/A (MiMo hand-rolled bcrypt/has_secure_password auth, no devise). Catalog fallback `nokogiri 1.13.5` is unresolvable here (the Rails 8.1 tree pins nokogiri high via rails-html-sanitizer -> loofah; downgrading to 1.13.5 conflicts). Per the catalog equivalent-target rule I used the established strong-alternate `puma 6.4.1` (CVE-2024-21647) — the SAME parity choice as ALL six B300 precedents (nex_n25_pro, glm_5_3_full, deepseek_v4_1_flash, minimax_m3_1_flash, kimi_k2_thinking, qwen38_flash_next). Severity recorded High 3 (uniform; denominator-40 parity).
